english.html: Together with the said Pierre Guerre, uncle of the said Martin.

There was great reason to dismiss this poor Pierre Guerre from the case and suit; who, so far from deserving to be punished, was worthy of recompense, and merited double praise for a work so good, so virtuous and so charitable, as to have spent part of his property and exposed his person to great peril and danger of his life, to uncover this deed and bring so prodigious an imposture to light.
And has remanded, and remands, the said du Tilh to the said Judge of Rieux, to have this present decision put into execution according to its form and tenor.

It was fitting to remand the execution of the decision to the Judge of Rieux, who had not spared himself in searching out, by all honest means of Justice, the truth of this deed. Added to which, it greatly befits the dignity of the sovereign courts to maintain and preserve the authority of the inferior ones <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, and so to act that, by their example and for the public good, all Judges (each in his degree) be by all and everywhere revered, as our Laws also often command <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>.

notes.citation: Code 7.64 (Quando provocare non est necesse), l. Omnem (fragment not identified); Decretals, X 2.28 (De appellationibus), c. Ut debitus (Lateran IV, c. 35; cf. X 2.28.59, chapter number not verified)
notes.original: l. omnẽ. C. quand. prouo non eſt nece. c. vt debitus. de appel.
notes.gloss: Ut debitus honor iudicibus et sedibus servetur — that due honour be kept to judges and their seats: the constitution restraining frivolous appeals from lower judges. The transcribers' e. for the siglum is read c., a chapter of the Decretals.

notes.citation: Digest 16.3 (Depositi vel contra), l. 1, § Casum (paragraph not verified); Digest 1.18 (De officio praesidis), l. Observandum (D. 1.18.19, Callistratus)
notes.original: l. i. P. caſum D. depoſiti l. obſeruandum D. de officio præſ.
notes.gloss: Callistratus: the magistrate dispensing justice must make himself easy of access but not suffer himself to be despised — contemni non patiatur. The transcribers' depoſt./depoſit. is the title Depositi abbreviated.
